title: Steering the Fidelity in State Preparation on Noisy Bosonic Systems with Risk-Seeking Optimization
authors: Riccardo Piantoni, Riccardo Pellini, Maurizio Ferrari Dacrema, Paolo Cremonesi
abstract: In order to execute quantum algorithms on bosonic quantum computers, it is necessary to encode their inputs into a desired target quantum state, with a process called state preparation. In real settings, state preparation methods operate in stochastic scenarios, where the prepared state is represented as a mixed state, that is a probabilistic ensemble of pure states. Therefore, existing state preparation methods optimize a variational ansatz by averaging over all possible sequences of photon loss events contained in the prepared ensemble, yielding an output state which approximates the desired target with a certain average fidelity. Such an approach, however, does not take into account directly the distribution of fidelities across states in the ensemble. In this work, we aim to maximize the fidelity of only a subset of pure states sampled from the prepared ensemble, at the cost of reducing the average fidelity overall. This trade-off is relevant when the goal is to obtain high-fidelity states with a certain probability, rather than maximizing the average fidelity of the prepared ensemble. We borrow and adapt objective functions from risk-sensitive optimization, a framework that optimizes specific characteristics of a distribution rather than only its expectation, and that has been successfully applied in Reinforcement Learning. In the considered experimental settings, our results show that the infidelities of some pure states in the prepared ensemble can be reduced by up to four orders of magnitude when using risk-seeking objectives, compared to those achieved using the standard optimization of the average fidelity. Furthermore, we show that it is possible to control the trade-off between the probability of obtaining high-fidelity states and the lowest infidelity threshold reached, providing the flexibility to select the operating point that best suits a certain application.
summary: This paper proposes using risk-seeking optimization to improve state preparation fidelity on noisy bosonic quantum computers. Instead of maximizing the average fidelity, the method optimizes for the probability of achieving high-fidelity states by analyzing individual noise trajectories. This approach yields substantial improvements in state quality metrics compared to traditional average fidelity optimization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitations of standard state preparation methods for bosonic quantum computers, which only optimize the average fidelity when noise is present.
main_result: Risk-seeking optimization techniques can significantly reduce the infidelities of specific pure states in the prepared ensemble by orders of magnitude compared to optimizing the average fidelity.
method: The authors adapt risk-sensitive optimization, using entropic risk measures, to optimize parameters by focusing on the distribution of fidelities across individual quantum noise trajectories rather than just their expectation value.
model_or_system: The study models state preparation on bosonic quantum systems (qudits) subjected to photon loss noise, utilizing the SNAP-Displacement (SD) protocol.
key_observables: Fidelity (pure-state and average), $\epsilon$-probability (probability of achieving a certain fidelity), and Success Rate (SR).
important_parameters: Risk coefficient ($ eta$), noise parameters like cavity decoherence time ($T_1$), and the number of SD-blocks ($B$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that optimizing trajectory-wise objectives using risk measures is superior to optimizing the expectation value of the fidelity.
figures_summary: The figures likely compare the performance metrics (e.g., $\epsilon$-probability vs. $ eta$) obtained using standard average fidelity optimization versus the proposed risk-seeking objectives, demonstrating the trade-off control.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem with average fidelity optimization, then introduces risk-seeking optimization via entropic risk measures, details the Monte Carlo estimation of gradients for trajectory-wise objectives, and finally presents comparative results showing the benefits and trade-offs of different risk objectives.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the practical challenge of noise in quantum computation by providing a mathematically rigorous framework (risk-sensitive optimization) to control the probability distribution of state quality, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.
